findings.title: 0x9361 carries geometry (dim1) - the 'read/write asymmetry' is a probe artifact
findings.handoff_says: 0x9361 (read) is a fixed template - byte-identical across shapes and counts (write carries geometry, read just reads).
findings.repo_shows: The 0x9361 record contains dim1 at +0x0A (same offset as in 0x9365), the stride-class value at +0x18 (8,16,16,24,24,24,24,32,... same law as 0x9365 +0x1C) and dim1*16 at +0x4A and +0x4E. It only ignores dim0 (+0x0E is the constant 81920). The spec's cmp probe (gen_states_width 1 4 vs 1 8) varies only dim0, the one dimension the read record ignores, so it cannot falsify the claim.
findings.evidence: $WD/gen_shape.py 4 D1, N=1, h17, u32 at +0x0a/+0x18/+0x4a: dim1=2: 2/0x8/0x20; 3: 3/0x10/0x30; 4: 4/0x10/0x40; 5: 5/0x18/0x50; 8: 8/0x18/0x80; 9: 9/0x20/0x90; 24: 24/0x20/0x180; 64: 64/0x20/0x400. Every one of those records differs from the dim1=4 record; dim0=2,4,8,16,64 at dim1=8 gives identical +0x0a=8,+0x0e=81920,+0x18=0x18. Also dim0=1 produces two 0x9361 and zero 0x9365.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate: 0x9361 is dim0-independent but carries dim1, the stride-class field and a per-state slot word; drop 'fixed template' and the geometry-asymmetry narrative. Add a spec line comparing 0x9361 for [4,4] vs [4,8] (they must differ at +0x0A) and make the cmp test explicit about which dimension it varies.

findings.title: 0x9365 stride law min(2*dim1+8,32) is wrong at most dim1; stride is 8*min(ceil(log2 dim1),4)
findings.handoff_says: stride = min(2*dim1+8, 32) at +0x1c; saturates at 32 (for dim1>=12).
findings.repo_shows: The law matches only at dim1=4, 8, 12 and the saturated range. Observed strides 8,16,16,24,24,24,24,32,... for dim1=2..9+ fit 8*min(ceil(log2(dim1)),4) on all 22 measured dim1. Saturation starts at dim1=9. The repo's generators (gen_states.py, gen_states_width.py) never vary dim1, so the spec checks one point (stride=16 at dim1=4). dim1=1 and dim1=16 produce no 0x9365 (dim1=16 emits 0x9360+0x9364).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the law with the measured table (or the log2 fit labelled empirical). Add spec lines at dim1=2, 5 and 9 (strides 8, 24, 32) using a shape generator that varies dim1. Document the dim1=1/16 and dim0=1 variants. Do not claim 'fully decoded'.

findings.title: 0x9365 region (+0x48) = dim1 MiB only in the last (short-form) record; N>=2 programs use a long form with 1 MiB at +0x48
findings.handoff_says: region = dim1 x 1 MiB (+0x48, x4 slots).
findings.repo_shows: Two 0x9365 layouts. Short form (N=1, and the last 0x9365 in the file for N>=2): words +0x44=1 MiB, +0x48,+0x4c,+0x50 = dim1 MiB (3 slots). Long form (the other N-1 records): +0x44 dim1 MiB, +0x48 = 1 MiB, +0x4c,+0x50,+0x54 dim1 MiB. decode_9365.py reads the first record, so for the standard 53-state program (and on both h16g and h17) it prints region=1048576, not dim1 MiB (4194304). The spec only decodes N=1.
findings.evidence: gen_shape_n.py N 4 D1 words at +0x40..+0x54 in MiB: N=2 D1=8: rec0 [.,8,1,8,8,8], rec1 [.,1,8,8,8,tag]; N=3 D1=4: two [.,4,1,4,4,4] then [.,1,4,4,4,tag]. gen_states_width 53 4: region@+0x48 distribution {1048576: 52, 4194304: 1}. `python3 scripts/decode_9365.py` on gen_states 53 1 1: 'dim0=4 dim1=4 stride=16 region=1048576' (h16g and h17).
findings.suggested_fix: State that +0x48 is dim1 MiB only in the short form; describe the long/short forms and which state gets which; make decode_9365.py (and the spec) decode a chosen record index or all records.

findings.title: 0x9361 is not count-independent: first record differs from N=1, other records embed a per-state slot word
findings.handoff_says: byte-identical across shapes and counts.
findings.repo_shows: N distinct 0x9361 bodies in an N-state program. Record 0 differs from the N=1 record at byte +0x3a (0x72 vs 0x71); records 1..N-1 use a second template and carry (slot_index<<8)|(copy<<7) as a u16 at +0x4c (slot ids 0x23..0x3d).
findings.evidence: $WD/mtool.py cmp9361 w1_4.macho w53_4.macho -> 'B records identical to A[0]: 0/53'; `python3 scripts/cmp_9361.py` on the same pair exits 'bodies differ across programs'. rec1..rec52 differ from each other only at +0x4c/+0x4d (e.g. 0x3280,0x2e80,...,0x2300,0x3d00). N=2,3,10,53: distinct bodies == record count.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'identical across dim0 only'. Mention the slot word in 0x9361 and extend the spec to compare per-state records.

findings.title: M4->M5 'identical, only delta is one extra 0x934a' is false at record-content level
findings.handoff_says: The same 53-state program for h16g and h17 is identical - same counts, same slot model, same 54 cap. The only delta: h17 emits one extra 0x934a record.
findings.repo_shows: Counts, slot decode and the 54 cap are the same (confirmed), but no 0x9361/0x9365/0x9344/0x9442 record is byte-identical between arches. Constant per-arch fields differ in every record (see evidence). Mach-O cpusubtype (7 vs 9), __text size (+16) and ModelMaxDramUsage also differ.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'record counts, slot model and the 54 cap are identical; contents differ by arch constants (list); h17 adds one 0x934a'. Rule out 'portable' wording for byte-level consumers.

findings.title: Open thread 2: payload 0x21 (33) is arch-specific, not constant; it is 0x31 (49) on h16g
findings.handoff_says: The embedded children (0x934a, 0x1340, 0x1341, 0x1440) carry constant payload 0x21 (33) across all shapes; why 33?
findings.repo_shows: On h17 the 0x1440 payload byte is 0x21 (54 records) / 0xe1 (53); on h16g it is 0x31 (54) / 0xf1 (53). The constant moves by 0x10 between M4 and M5, like the 0x10->0x20 fields in 0x9361/0x9365, so it looks like a hardware-generation field rather than a count/type constant.
findings.evidence: Histogram of byte +4 of every 0x1440 record in gen_states 53 1 1: h16g {49:54, 241:53}; h17 {33:54, 225:53}. Differences listed in the M4->M5 finding.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite thread 2 as 'payload is 0x31 on h16g, 0x21 on h17 (hardware-generation field?)' and test on other arches before searching for a count/type meaning.

findings.title: 0x9442 family is outputs+2N (== __data section count), not 2N+1
findings.handoff_says: It's the 2N+1 segment family (107 records at 53 states, matching __data segments).
findings.repo_shows: Count == plain outputs + 2N in every program. 2N+1 coincides only when exactly one plain output exists, and contradicts the handoff's own H51 formula. Plain inputs do not contribute.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'one 0x9442 per __data section = outputs + 2N' and add (52,1,50)->154 to the spec.

findings.title: A frontend io cap does exist: declared in+out <= 255 (MaxLiveInLiveOutExceeded)
findings.handoff_says: io-port budget is execution-time, NOT frontend; the ANECCompile frontend accepts 200+ io ports.
findings.repo_shows: validate/compile reject any program with declared in+out >= 256 ('status=0x1 rc=1 error: MaxLiveInLiveOutExceeded'); 128/128 fails (the 'frontend accepts 128' reading of the spec's 64/64 comment is wrong). The spec header and master writeup say 'no frontend constraint'. The handoff omits the limit the repo's own reconciliation doc records.
findings.evidence: milc ane validate --arch h17 on gen_mix_ports: 254/1 ok, 255/1 FAIL, 1/254 ok, 1/255 FAIL, 100/155 ok, 100/156 FAIL, 150/105 ok, 150/106 FAIL, 128/128 FAIL, 127/128 ok. `milc ane run` hits the same wall as 'ANECCompile() FAILED' (128/128, 1/255) but prunes dead inputs (256/1 and 1000/1 run fine), so validate and run differ on unused inputs.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'two budgets: frontend declared in+out <= 255 (MaxLiveInLiveOutExceeded), then execution live_in+out <= 127'. Add a spec pair (127,128 ok / 128,128 fail) and reconcile with docs/evidence/reconciliation-two-port-limits.md.

findings.title: Spec 'passes' assertions are vacuous; only the failing halves test anything
findings.handoff_says: docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.spec has executable assertions for all of it; if a claim is wrong the harness should catch it.
findings.repo_shows: `want_out_re  step 0:` matches the failure message 'milc ane run: step 0: execute_sync -> 11 ... Program Inference error' too, and want_rc is never used. A regression that lowered the cap (e.g. in=1 out=126 starting to fail) would still pass its 'passes' line.
findings.evidence: `python3 scripts/gen_mix_ports.py 1 127 > f.mil; milc ane run f.mil --steps 1 2>&1` -> rc=1; `grep -qE 'step 0:'` on that output returns a match (same for (65,64),(80,64),(100,64)). Genuine pass output starts a line with 'step 0: 767µs' and rc=0.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `want_out_re  ^step 0: [0-9]` and/or `want_rc 0` on every pass line; keep `want_out Inference error` on fail lines.

findings.title: Per-state triple and 54-cap model is shape-dependent for the copy records (omission); the 54 cap itself is shape-independent
findings.handoff_says: Per state: 1x 0x9344 + 1x 0x9361 + 1x 0x9365; the descriptor table caps at 54.
findings.repo_shows: Record families depend on state shape: dim0=1 -> 2x 0x9361 and no 0x9365; dim1=16 -> 0x9360+0x9364; dim1=1 -> none. Regardless, 0x9344 = N+1 and 54 states always fails ('unable to allocate free BAR'), which supports the table-cap explanation.
findings.suggested_fix: Note which shapes follow the 0x9361/0x9365 pair, and that decoders only handle that pair.

findings.title: Terminology: '__data segments' are sections; 'outputs' excludes state-update returns and inputs
findings.handoff_says: __data segments = outputs + 2 x states; 107 records matching __data segments.
findings.repo_shows: The 107 are __data sections inside __FVMLIB LC_SEGMENT_64s; at 53 states there are only 54 __data-bearing LC_SEGMENT_64s (53 singletons + one segment holding 54 sections), a number equal to the 0x9344 record count. 'outputs' counts only plain outputs (gen_states 53 1 1 returns 54 tensors but yields 107).
findings.evidence: $WD/segsum.py: (53,1,1) 57 LC_SEGMENT_64; (52,1,50) 56 with one 102-section segment holding 154 total sections; (10,*) all single-section. $WD/layout.py shows __FVMLIB.__data sections.
findings.suggested_fix: Say '__data sections (plain outputs + 2N)'; optionally record that segments hit 54 at the cap, a candidate alternative reading of 'WHY 54' worth distinguishing from the 0x9344 table.

findings.title: Decoder scripts misparse section_64 (size/offset read from addr/size fields)
findings.handoff_says: count_desc_records.py and the other decoders scan only the __text section.
findings.repo_shows: scripts/count_desc_records.py, decode_9365.py, decode_slot_word.py read section size at +32 and offset at +40, but section_64 puts addr at +32, size at +40, offset at +48. They actually scan [low32(size), EOF), and cmp_9361.py hard-codes 0x50C0. Harmless on every macho measured (identical counts to true __text and 0 hits in load commands), but the 'only __text' guarantee is false.
findings.evidence: $WD/layout.py: 53-state __TEXT.__text addr=0x301ac000 size=0x4ff0 offset=0x64000 vs script-read size=0x301ac000 off=0x4ff0; $WD/analyze.py true_text == repo_method == whole_file counts for 9344/9361/9365/9442/934a on 5 machos.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the offsets (+40/+48) or drop the 'only __text' comment; stop hard-coding 0x50C0.

findings.title: Slot table: 'each slot holding 2 records' is not what the data shows
findings.handoff_says: The table is an array of slots each holding 2 records.
findings.repo_shows: Slots hold up to two records distinguished by the copy bit. N=1: 2 slots, 0 full; N=3: 3 slots, 1 full; N=53: 28 slots, 26 full (the spec's own numbers imply 2 half slots).
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'up to 2 records per slot (copy bit)'.

findings.repo_shows: vendor/mil_spec contains 8 files that are not in pristine upstream plus patches 0001-0017. The vendor-guard CI check only compares the tree with vendor/manifest.sha256, so it passes (OK, 442 files). --rebuild syncs the pristine+patches tree over vendor/mil_spec with rsync --delete, so it would remove these files. The PROBE-3 spec (docs/spec/shape-flex-matrix.spec:8,22-61) builds and runs 6 of them, and the A.5 and RUN-2 evidence cites e5_dual_path.rs and probe_run2_state.rs.
findings.evidence: Scratch rebuild: git clone upstream; git checkout 20f097f; patch -p1 for 0001..0017; 'diff -rq <scratch>/up vendor/mil_spec -x target' -> 'Only in vendor/.../crates/mil_infer/examples: cml_exec.rs, e5_dual_path.rs, e5exec.rs, mk_minflex.rs, predseg.rs, probe_run2_state.rs, seg4.rs, shape_flex_e5rt.rs'. 'rsync -a --delete -n --itemize-changes --exclude target --exclude manifest.sha256 <scratch>/up/ vendor/mil_spec/' printed 8 '*deleting crates/mil_infer/examples/...' lines (dry run). grep -c of those names in vendor/manifest.sha256 = 8. apply-patches.sh:80-81. Introducing commits: b85b6fd (6 files), d4579a7, 26447d2. --rebuild itself was not run. The repo is unchanged (git status clean apart from an untracked scripts/__pycache__).
findings.suggested_fix: Warn: do not run --rebuild until these 8 files are covered by a patch (for example 0018 probe-examples) or moved out of vendor/ (the repo-root examples/ is unowned; see the OWNERSHIP gap). Until then use 'apply-patches.sh --check' plus 'vendor-guard.sh --verify'. Also record that --verify proves tree == manifest, not tree == pristine + patches, and consider adding a rebuild-and-diff step to CI.

findings.title: Patch procedure omits how a patch is produced, the stacking baseline, and the real two-commit manifest sequence
findings.handoff_says: A patch, a PATCHES.md entry, a FORK(ane-stack) comment and a regenerated manifest (from a clean tree), then rebuild with --rebuild.
findings.repo_shows: (1) PATCHES.md:45-51 names the root cause of the 0007/0008/0010 defects: patches written from prose instead of a committed diff. The method that does not recur is 'edit the tree, commit, then git diff HEAD~1 -- <paths> | sed ... into patches/, confirm with --check'. (2) docs/evidence/0006-double-patch-and-stacking.md ('Process change (permanent)') requires diffing against pristine plus all lower-numbered patches, never the raw working tree. (3) Practice is two commits: patch plus tree, then a separate 'sync manifest' commit (12 such commits, e.g. 17abc42 follows 6409cf6, 15875c6 follows 26447d2). This contradicts 0006's 'commit patch + manifest together' and vendor-guard.sh:86-88, because --generate refuses an uncommitted tree. (4) --rebuild already calls --generate (apply-patches.sh:81), so it is not a separate step, and it aborts when the rebuilt tree differs from HEAD. (5) When another lane has uncommitted files in the tree, --generate is blocked and the manifest entries were edited by hand (880cf12). (6) ENGINEERING.md:95 requires vendor patches to be separate commits from our own code.
findings.evidence: PATCHES.md:45-51; docs/evidence/0006-double-patch-and-stacking.md ('Process change (permanent)' steps 1-7); scripts/apply-patches.sh:4-6,80-81; scripts/vendor-guard.sh:55-63,86-88; git log --format=%s | grep -ci 'sync.*manifest' -> 12; 880cf12 body.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the one-line rule with the actual sequence: edit and commit the tree plus patch plus PATCHES.md, derive the patch from git diff HEAD~1 (vendor-relative paths) against pristine plus lower patches, run apply-patches.sh --check, then vendor-guard.sh --generate on the clean tree and commit the manifest separately. State that 'dirty' means uncommitted or untracked files under vendor/mil_spec only.

findings.title: The '--generate refuses a dirty tree' safeguard is silently disabled in a linked git worktree
findings.handoff_says: 'regenerated vendor/manifest.sha256 (from a clean tree - the --generate guard refuses a dirty one)'
findings.repo_shows: vendor-guard.sh:55 wraps the clean-tree check in 'if [ -d "$root/.git" ]'. In a linked worktree .git is a file, not a directory, so the check is skipped and --generate hashes whatever is on disk. This session's own worktree is one, and the project clearly runs agent sessions in worktrees.
findings.evidence: 'ls -ld .git' -> '-rw-r--r-- ... .git' and 'cat .git' -> 'gitdir: <repo>/.git/worktrees/review-handoff-doc-953eea'; test -d .git is false. The primary checkout <repo>/.git is a directory. Introduced by 457f714. Not executed because the unit forbids --generate.
findings.suggested_fix: Tell the successor to run --generate only from the primary checkout, or change the test to 'git rev-parse --git-dir' / '[ -e "$root/.git" ]'.

findings.evidence: `grep -qE -- 'step 0:' <<< 'milc ane run: step 0: ANEProgramProcessRequestDirect() Failed with status=0x2 : statusType=0x9: Program Inference error'` -> rc=0 (string test only; no hardware run). findings.title: decode_slot_word.py assumes the model and cannot detect violations; the word is really a contiguous index with a hole
findings.handoff_says: slot word = (slot_index << 8) | (copy << 7) - the table is an array of slots each holding 2 records; not the slot-id space (56 record capacity).
findings.repo_shows: The script hard-codes the field slicing and set()-dedups, so sio prints 'slots=28 fullcopies=26' for 85 records. Data: w = 0x2300 + 0x80*k with states k=0..N-1, header k=N+1, k=N unused (verified on d1, d53, m52, w256, sio). Consequences: writeup L195 'slots = ceil(records/2)' fails at its own rows N=1 (2 slots) and N=53 (28 vs 27); L196-197 'the two records in a full slot are a state's two descriptors' contradicts one record per state; L193 labels '0x3d header' but the header is 0x3e00 (0x3d00 is a state, k=52). 28 slots x 2 = 56 vs 54 records is explained by the two unused coordinates k=53 and k=55; N=54 would need k=55, which only fits if 0x3e80 is valid - never observed.
findings.evidence: scratchpad kmodel.py/single.py over /tmp/pl_d1c, pl_d53c, pl_m52c, pl_w256c, pl_siocc: k sets as above; singletons d53 {0x3d:[0], 0x3e:[0]}, m52 {0x3d:[1]}.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the word as an index k=(w-0x2300)/0x80 with a one-slot gap before the header; make the script assert (not assume) low-7-bits==0, no duplicate (slot,copy) among state records, and report multiplicity; fix the writeup rows.

findings.title: Descriptor scanners mis-parse the section header and scan the whole file, contrary to their docstring
findings.handoff_says: Decoders: count_desc_records.py, decode_9365.py, decode_slot_word.py, cmp_9361.py
findings.repo_shows: text_file_range() reads size at section_64+32 (that is addr) and offset at +40 (that is the low 32 bits of size); real layout is addr@32, size@40, offset@48. For pl_d1 it returns (0x2c0, 0x300102c0) though __text is at 0x8000 size 0x2c0. The scan therefore runs from the section SIZE value to EOF over every 2-byte-aligned word (inside load commands for small files), not 'only the __text section' as the docstring and c7273c1 claim; cmp_9361.py hard-codes 0x50C0. No false positives on the 7 binaries tested (whole-file == true-__text counts), but any 0x9344/0x9365 word in __const/weights would be miscounted.
findings.evidence: scratchpad hdr.py/truetext.py: 'script-read size=0x30010000 off=0x2c0' vs real 'size=0x2c0 off=0x8000'; tag counts in true __text equal whole-file counts for 0x9344/0x9361/0x9365/0x934a in d1, d53, sio, m52, w256, mm(h16g), mm(h17).
findings.suggested_fix: Use +40 for size and +48 for offset (and fix the same copy in the other three scripts); remove the hard-coded 0x50C0.

findings.repo_shows: The 54 figure is an artifact of every spec generator using exactly one plain input. 0x9344 count = #states + #plain inputs on every retained binary. Programs with far more than 54 0x9344 records compile fine; the invariant is the state count (53). The '+1' is the input descriptor, not a state-triggered header (a 0-state program still has 1 record).
findings.evidence: (1) Spec L60-61 asserts 53 states + 32 in + 32 out compiles; its output /tmp/pl_siocc/pl_sio.macho gives 'python3 scripts/count_desc_records.py /tmp/pl_siocc/pl_sio.macho' -> '0x9344 records: 85'; decode_slot_word.py -> 'records=85 slots=28 fullcopies=26' (all 85 real: 32 of them share slot word 0x3e00). (2) /tmp/s0c/s0.macho (0 states, 1 in, 1 out; /tmp/s0.mil) -> '0x9344 records: 1', versus writeup L148-158 (0 at 0 states, '+1 present only when at least one state exists'). (3) /tmp/hw/st53/st53.macho (53 read-only [4,32] states + 4 inputs; /tmp/hw/st53.mil) -> 57 records and compiled; /tmp/hw/st54 and st55 only left additional_weights.bin (no macho; BAR message not retained). (4) /tmp/threec/three.macho (3 states, 3 inputs) -> 6 records, 4 slots (0x23,0x24,0x26,0x27), not ceil(6/2). (5) records - states = inputs holds for s0, s1, pa4, three, st53, pl_d53, pl_m52 (53 = 52+1), pl_sio (85 = 53+32), pl_w256 (54). Since records == states+1 in every spec case, no spec case can distinguish 'cap = 54 records' from 'cap = 53 states'; pl_sio does, and it favours states.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite H53/H57/H101: the cap is 53 independent state<> params; 0x9344 records = states + plain inputs (the single x0 is the '+1'); the 54-record coincidence is a generator artifact; slots != ceil(records/2). Mark 'WHY 54' as open or as 'reformulated', not resolved. Say 'the table has 28 slots / 54 records in the 1-input family', never '54 slots'. Add a spec case counting 0x9344 on gen_states.py 53 32 32 (expect 85) so the next agent cannot re-derive the wrong cap. Next probe: state-slot occupancy (coordinates 0x23..0x3d x 2 copies = 54, with (0x3d,copy1) referenced by every 0x9442 child) as the real 53 limit.
